Introduction Issue resolution systems, which automatically resolve bug reports or feature requests in code repositories, are useful. They are also challenging to build, because issue descriptions tend to be informal and code repositories are often large and complex ( Jimenez et al., 2024 ) . Several issue resolution systems leverage tests: for code candidate selection in parallel inference scaling ( Arora et al., 2024 ; Gao et al., 2025 ; Jain et al., 2025 ; Ruan et al., 2024 ; Xia et al., 2025 ; Zhang et al., 2025 ) , code r

l., 2024 ; Xia et al., 2025 ; Zhang et al., 2025 ) , code refinement in sequential inference scaling ( Chen et al., 2024 ; Li et al., 2025b ; Yang et al., 2024 ; Zhang et al., 2024 ) , or both ( Ehrlich et al., 2025 ; Li et al., 2025c ) . These systems rely upon the implicit premise that tests offer a reliable signal in this setting. Unfortunately, little is known about whether this premise holds. To the contrary, startling results in adjacent settings cast doubt upon it ( Baker et al., 2025 ; Smith et al., 2015 ; Stroebl et al., 2024 ) . Relying upon tests for issue resolution can cause test overfitting : generated code that narrowly passes the observed tests but breaks other functionality. This paper empirically investigates the problem of test overfitting in repository-level issue resolution, on benchmarks such as SWE-bench ( Jimenez et al., 2024 ) . We extend these systems with a test-based code refinement loop that is representative of those found in recent work ( Ehrlich et al., 2025 ; Li et al., 2025c ; Li et al., 2025b ; Li et al., 2025a ) . The experiments are based on the TDD-bench Verified ( Ahmed et al., 2024 ) benchmark for test-driven development, which is derived from SWE-bench ( Jimenez et al., 2024 ) . TDD-bench Verified comprises challenging real-world Python issue resolution tasks. This paper makes the following contributions. • It measures the degree of test overfitting by LLMs in repository-level issue resolution tasks. • It describes techniques to reduce overfitting and reports how they impact both overfitting and performance. • It also includes a limit study of how much an oracle with access to the hidden golden tests could help performance. This paper demonstrates that test overfitting is a clear problem in modern LLM-based issue resolution systems. And unfortunately, while attempts to mitigate this overfitting do work to some extent, they also reduce effectiveness on the original task of issue resolution. E
